name: Yasen
description: Divine guardian of the ash tree and spirit of spring's return to the forest. Governs healing and the World Tree.
mythology: Yasen is the divine personification and guardian spirit of the ash tree — 'yasen' is the Slavic word for ash. The ash is one of the most sacred trees in Slavic and Indo-European tradition; in some Slavic variants, the World Tree is an ash rather than an oak. Yasen embodies the return of life to the forest in spring — the greening of ash trees being one of the surest signs winter has fully passed. He governs the healing properties of ash wood: ash bark, leaves, and the winged seeds (keys) were used extensively in Slavic folk medicine for wounds, snake bites, and fevers. He is a gentle, renewal-focused deity of woodland places.

offerings: First spring flowers tied to ash branches
